comparison: Perfect agreement on CIA model efficacy data (C8, C31-C35, C41, C49). Both evaluations find the antigen-specific therapeutic effect in collagen-induced arthritis convincing, with appropriate controls and experimental design.

Strong agreement on drug sequestration and release mechanism (C5, C19-C24). Both evaluations find the evidence for DC accumulation and release of FK506 convincing, including inhibitor experiments, ELISA measurements, and antibody depletion studies.

Agreement on in vitro characterization of FKDC inhibitory effects (C3, C4, C18, C59, C60). Both evaluations accept the evidence that FK506-loaded DCs reduce T cell proliferation and IFN-γ responses while maintaining normal DC phenotype.

Agreement on T cell apoptosis mechanism (C6, C25-C27, C50). Both evaluations accept the flow cytometry data showing increased annexin V staining and reduced bcl-xl expression in divided T cells, supporting the antigen-specific targeting mechanism.

Agreement on IL2 rescue experiments (C7, C28-C30). Both evaluations accept that IL2 supplementation restores T cell survival, bcl-xl expression, and IFN-γ production, confirming the mechanism operates through IL2 deprivation.

Agreement on background and contextual claims (C1, C2, C10-C13). Both evaluations accept the established facts about FK506's mechanism of action, therapeutic applications, and adverse effects as appropriately cited.
Agreement on background literature regarding other immunosuppressants (C14-C16). Both evaluations accept the cited prior work on rapamycin and mycophenolate effects on DCs as appropriate context.

Disagreement on reduced systemic exposure claims (C36, C37, C42, C61, C62). OpenEval finds the functional assays sufficient to demonstrate reduced systemic drug exposure. Peer reviewers require direct comparative evidence at equivalent therapeutic efficacy levels, noting the comparison was not done properly.

Disagreement on toxicity reduction claims (C38, C39, C43, C63, C64). OpenEval accepts the serum chemistry data showing reduced pancreatic toxicity but notes limited treatment duration. Peer reviewers require comparative evidence at equivalent therapeutic efficacy, stating safety advantages are 'not actually shown.'

Agreement on uncertainty regarding FKBP mechanism (C44-C46). Both evaluations note the mechanism is speculative. OpenEval states direct measurement would strengthen conclusions; peer reviewers explicitly require knockdown experiments to validate the FKBP-mediated accumulation hypothesis.

Agreement on speculative nature of broader applications (C47, C48). Both evaluations recognize these claims about extending to other cell types or drugs are hypothetical and lack experimental validation.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding dose calculations (C51-C53, C54). Both evaluations acknowledge the dose comparison but express concerns. OpenEval notes extrapolation uncertainties from in vitro to in vivo. Peer reviewers accept the calculation but require comparative efficacy data to validate safety claims.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding clinical translation (C9, C54-C56). Both evaluations find the concept promising but note limitations. OpenEval cites limited toxicity assessment and single disease model. Peer reviewers require additional comparative efficacy/safety data and mechanistic validation before clinical potential can be fully validated.
